title: operational-blueprint-access-and-vendor-procedures-2028
author: Marissa Gomez
body:
Overview:

This operational blueprint consolidates company-wide policies and step-by-step processes for access & permissions, change management, data stewardship, procurement & expenses, vendor lifecycle, travel approvals, and reusable internal templates. The goal is to provide a single reference for consistent decision-making, minimize operational risk, and speed routine approvals while preserving appropriate controls.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and third-party vendors that interact with company systems or data.
- Purpose-built for corporate and product-facing functions: engineering, product, finance, people-ops, security, and sales.
- Exclusions: Classified customer-specific contracts that explicitly override internal processes are covered under separate customer-specific runbooks.

Principles:
1. Least privilege: grant only the minimum rights required for the job and review quarterly.
2. Separation of duties: approvals and provisioning must be distinct when financial or data risk is non-trivial.
3. Auditability: every change and vendor relationship must have an auditable trail (owner, approver, rationale).
4. Risk-based flexibility: low-risk, high-velocity workflows are automated; high-risk actions require multi-level approvals.

1) Access & Permissions

Purpose: Standardize onboarding, offboarding, entitlement changes, and privileged access reviews.

Key Roles and Owners:
- Requester: person initiating a request for access.
- Approver: direct manager for role-based increases; resource owner for product access.
- IAM Owner: Security team (IAM) — enforces provisioning and periodic reviews.
- HR/People-ops: owns onboarding and offboarding triggers.

Standard access lifecycle:
1. Request: via Access Request form (Template: ACCESS-REQ-2026). Requests must include business justification and anticipated duration.
2. Approval: Manager approves requests under $7,500-equivalent risk (see approval matrix); resource owner approves all product or production environment access.
3. Provisioning: IAM Owner provisions via automation where possible and records the ticket ID.
4. Review: Quarterly entitlement review for privileged groups (admin, DB write, infra deploy).
5. Deprovisioning: Offboarding must revoke all tokens, cloud IAM roles, and third-party app access within 4 hours of termination notification.

Access approval matrix (text table):
| Resource sensitivity | Typical approver(s) | Escalation |
| Low (docs, wiki) | Manager | None |
| Medium (non-prod infra, analytics) | Manager + Resource Owner | Security on doubt |
| High (production infra, PII stores) | Manager + Resource Owner + Security | VP of Engineering / Legal |

Privileged access example CLI snippet (for audit log):
- Audit entry JSON example:
  {
    "actor": "alice@example.com",
    "action": "grant_role",
    "role": "db-admin",
    "resource": "prod-db-01",
    "request_id": "REQ-2026-1234"
  }

2) Change Management

Objective: Reduce risk from configuration and software changes while enabling frequent safe releases.

Change types:
- Standard Change: Pre-authorized, well-documented, repeatable (e.g., scheduled model refresh, schema migrations with automation).
- Normal Change: Requires review and approval (e.g., configuration changes to runtime, infra scaling policy changes).
- Emergency Change: Applied to restore service but must be documented and reviewed post-facto.

Process (normal change):
1. Submit Change Request in Change Log (fields: title, scope, rollback plan, test plan, owner, scheduled window).
2. Risk assessment: Low/Medium/High — if High, require security and service owner approval.
3. CAB Review (weekly): changes classified as Medium/High are reviewed by the Change Advisory Board (CAB). CAB composition: Eng lead, SRE, Security, Product representative, Finance (if cost impact).
4. Implementation: follow runbook, notify stakeholders via #infra-changes channel.
5. Post-Change Review: within 3 business days document outcome and any incidents.

Emergency change workflow:
- Implement emergency fix with a designated emergency implementer, notify on-call and Security, and open a retrospective ticket within 24 hours. All emergency changes require a root-cause and rollback improvement plan.

Change windows and SLOs:
- Standard change maintenance window: Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC.
- Target change success rate: 99.0% for scheduled changes (no production impact).

3) Data Management and Governance

Core policies:
- Classification: Data must be labeled as Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted.
- Data minimization: collect only the attributes required for the stated purpose.
- Retention: default internal data retention is 3 years unless otherwise required by law or contract.
- Encryption: at rest and in transit for Confidential and Restricted classes.

Access controls and approvals:
- PII and Restricted datasets require Data Owner + Security approval and must use approved tooling (see Appendix: Approved Data Stores).
- Data access requests follow same request/approval/provisioning lifecycle as general access but include an explicit justification and DB query plan for analytics projects.

Data incident response:
1. Detect: log or user report.
2. Contain: revoke access tokens, isolate affected systems.
3. Assess: Security leads classification and customer/contract implications.
4. Notify: follow incident and breach notification timelines (legal and customer notifications in 72 hours when required).
5. Remediate: patch, rotate keys, run a focused postmortem.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Principles:
- Centralize vendor procurement via the Procurement team for recurring expenses and significant one-offs.
- Empower teams to make low-dollar purchases with constrained thresholds and pre-approved vendors.

Approval tiers (text table):
| Spend bracket (USD) | Required approvals | Proc owner |
| < 500 | Requester's manager | Team lead handles purchase |
| 500–5,000 | Manager + Finance approval | Procurement coordinates PO |
| 5,000–50,000 | Manager + Finance + Legal (if contract) | Procurement issues the PO |
| > 50,000 | VP-level approval + Legal review | Procurement & Legal |

Procurement process (step-by-step):
1. Create a Purchase Request (PR) in the procurement system with estimated cost, vendor, justification, and account code.
2. Procurement validates vendor (AML/sanctions check) and issues a PO when appropriate.
3. Finance confirms chart of accounts and processes invoices for payment terms (standard Net 30 unless negotiated).
4. For software subscriptions, tag cost center and include auto-renewal reminders 60 days before renewal.

Expense policy highlights:
- Use company card for business travel when pre-approved; receipts required for all reimbursable expenses.
- Per diem: domestic $75/day, international $125/day unless explicit policy differs by country.
- Personal expenses are not reimbursable.

5) Vendor Management

Lifecycle stages: Selection -> Contracting -> Onboarding -> Monitoring -> Renewal/Offboarding.

Selection and contracting:
- Vendor selection requires at least two comparable quotes for purchases > $10k unless sole-source justification is documented.
- Legal must review contracts with data access, security, or SLAs.
- Standard security questions are required for vendors with system access (see Appendix B: Vendor Security Questionnaire).

Onboarding checklist:
1. Assign vendor owner (internal stakeholder).
2. Register vendor in Vendor Registry with contract metadata and renewal dates.
3. Provision scoped access with expiration and rotate shared credentials by default.
4. Schedule quarterly or semiannual vendor reviews depending on criticality.

Monitoring and KPIs:
- KPIs to track: uptime SLA compliance, incident response times, change windows, and annual security attestations.
- Critical vendors receive an annual business and security review; moderate vendors at least every 18 months.

Offboarding requirements:
- Terminate access, collect assets, preserve contract history, and retain data per retention policy.

6) Travel Policy (summary)

Booking and approvals:
- All business travel requires a Travel Request submitted at least 10 business days prior to travel.
- Manager approval required for travel; Finance must sign off for international travel with > $5,000 expected cost.

Allowed expenses and limits:
- Flights: economy for trips < 8 hours; premium economy or business for long-haul per HR policy exceptions.
- Hotels: mid-range business hotels; maximum nightly rate per city is published in the Travel Rates master list.
- Ground transport: use ride-shares or taxis; rental cars must be pre-approved.

Safety and duty of care:
- People-ops maintains travel advisories. For countries rated as high risk, manager + People-ops approval is required and additional safety planning must be submitted.

7) Templates & Internal Forms

Quick list of reusable templates (file names):
- ACCESS-REQ-2026 (Access Request)
- CHANGE-REQ-2026 (Change Request)
- PURCHASE-REQ-2027 (Purchase Request)
- VENDOR-ONBOARD-CHK (Vendor Onboarding Checklist)
- TRAVEL-REQ-2025 (Travel Request)

Examples: Purchase Request required fields (table style):
| Field | Required? | Notes |
| Requester | Yes | Person initiating purchase |
| Business justification | Yes | Tie to OKR or project code |
| Estimated cost | Yes | USD |
| Vendor name | Yes | Legal name for PO |
| Renewal terms | If recurring | Set reminders |

8) Governance, Reporting & Audit

- Quarterly governance review: Finance, Security, People-ops, and Procurement review top vendor spend, privileged accounts, and outstanding exceptions.
- Exceptions: document and escalate exceptions via the Policy Exceptions register; all exceptions auto-expire after 90 days unless renewed.
- Audit evidence: maintain change logs, access request tickets, PO records, and vendor contracts in the central records repository with retention aligned to the Data Management policy.

Appendices (references and checklists):
A. Approved Data Stores: list cloud DBs and analytics platforms (BigQuery, Redshift, Redwood-DataLake) and allowed use-cases.
B. Vendor Security Questionnaire: baseline checks (encryption, SOC reports, custom contract clauses).
C. Emergency change runbook: step-by-step rollback commands and contact matrix.

Revision history and ownership:
- Document owner: Marissa Gomez, Finance & Legal Operations.
- Review cadence: annual or when material changes occur.
- Change log: 2025-06-15 initial publication; 2026-10-02 updated vendor review cadence and procurement thresholds.
